text:
Beckett Sennecke is 20 years old, playing 20:23 a night and producing 1.24 points a game. For context, forwards picked in the top five since 2005 scored a median 0.54 a game in their first full season. This is his second, and Anaheim has handed him the keys: he's on the ice for 83% of the team's power-play chances, up from 47%.

Some of it is luck, and our numbers are blunt about how much. With him on the ice, Anaheim has scored 13 more goals than its chances deserve, the kind of on-ice shooting that fades, and his own shooting sits at 22.6%. At five on five the Ducks get 47.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, so the process trails the points. The real part shows in how he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey put his offensive impact in the 97th percentile, with a defensive cost to match. The skating and the puck carrying are what to watch once the bounces even out.
